dedupe_keys.name: modeling green stormwater infrastructure at the watershed scale in the salt lake valley

description: Modeling Green Stormwater Infrastructure at the Watershed-Scale in the Salt Lake Valley is a data set listed in HydroShare, an online repository for hydrology data and models, published or maintained by Prudencio, Liana (deposited on HydroShare). Flood infrastructure that uses pipes and culverts, also called gray infrastructure, collects and conveys stormwater to receiving areas, typically oceans, inland lakes, and wetlands. Gray infrastructure increases stormwater runoff volume and exposure to pollutants and prevents infiltration to groundwater. Green infrastructure is increasingly proposed to reestablish ecosystem services that are lost from urban development. Coverage: not restricted to one place in the metadata. The resource was created 2020-07-13 and last updated 2020-07-14; HydroShare lists it as a composite resource. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: this record was written from the HydroShare metadata only, so the files and any paper they support were not opened, their current availability was not checked, and the abstract may lag the deposit. It can support infrastructure planning, operations and risk studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-hydroshare-infrastructure-resources.
